summary: Admit an approval-bound Russian Post standalone return shipment through the tenant-scoped API and operation receipt boundary.

impacts.evidence: The route resolves the active logistics account in the authenticated organization/workspace scope and uses a tenant-scoped operation receipt.
Names and addresses are request-scoped PII; only the normalized shipment result and digest-bound receipt are durable.
OpenAPI adds POST /logistics/returns/separate with required idempotency and approval headers and bounded address/value/name fields.
The operation adds no event contract and returns a normalized synchronous provider result.
A provider-neutral separate-return request, result port and capability are additive to SDK v1.
Existing operation_receipts persistence supports pending/completed normalized results; no migration is needed.
Runtime admission, account capability, approval and idempotency are default-deny and independently checked.
The route requires write-sensitive fulfillment.return.separate.create approval bound to all request options by digest.
The approval ID, digest and operation receipt preserve the privileged operation lineage without storing PII payload.
A fresh receipt owns the single remote call; completed replays do not call the provider and pending outcomes block blind retry.
The adapter uses fixed HTTPS egress to the documented Russian Post standalone-return endpoint and one bounded request item.
The API distinguishes accepted fresh results, completed replays and pending ambiguous outcomes without returning raw provider errors.
Disabling capability or runtime admission prevents new returns while existing receipt evidence remains available.
Deterministic connector, HTTPS transport, API approval/idempotency, runtime admission, OpenAPI, SDK and frontend checks cover the operation.
